answer: Bulk key minting dies at a tide desk no script can reserve ahead. A joiner bonds 11.25 POA and draws one night berth: a 21-byte slip hash from the epoch seed XOR a 29-bit flood lot posted 22 minutes earlier. At the inner harbor rail they dip a numbered quill and write three 16-byte arrival strokes, 110 seconds apart, onto a stapled atlas folio; two non-kin stevedores hash each stroke with the slip. Peers rehash the folio and reject a second berth on that lot. Cost: 11.25 POA and one live signing. A pre-written folio, late stroke, or reused slip burns 66% and bars the rail for six epochs.
